Theme 018 · Typography & graphic systems

Typographic Window Reveal

Giant numerals and words fill the square edge to edge and work as windows: the product UI plays inside the letterforms while the counters stay dark. Every scene change is a dive through a glyph; the facts live in small mono captions around the type.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Mask glyph — Manrope 800 at 340–900 px used as an SVG clipPath; the letterform is the window.
  • Inner scene — live product UI (dashboard tiles, the metric chart) playing inside the glyph.
  • Counter portal — the hole of a "0", "8" or "%" used as the tunnel for scene-to-scene dives.
  • Stroke echo — a 3 px outline of the same glyph offset behind it, teal normally and coral for the anomaly.
  • Corner caption — small mono lines carrying every fact the glyph can't (metric name, time, deploy).
  • Numeral lockup — the ending "0" (customers who noticed) holding the product, beside the tagline and CTA.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Zoom-through — mask scale 1 → 40 into a counter (power4.in, 700 ms), cutting on the drop or a downbeat at 120 BPM.
  • Parallax interior — the inner scene drifts at 0.3× the opposite way to the glyph, linear, so type and content never feel glued.
  • Glyph swap — one numeral clip-wipes to the next (1 → 0, 38 → 0) in 250 ms on the downbeat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

The number is the message and the product is literally inside it, so the frame reads at a glance and still shows real UI. It is cheap to build with a single clip mask per scene. Risk: content inside the letters is not readable as UI, so every fact must also appear in a caption.

Adapt to your product: pick the three numbers that tell your story (a pain count, your key metric, a zero) and put screen recordings or UI mock-ups inside them; keep the captions for the actual data.
